The experience taught Jack more than any book could. Little by little, things began to change. The school computer room has become an important part of daily life. In fact, the teacher fought her sleepiness during the dull webinar.

Jack thanked Tom for the honest advice. Jack wrote down every idea in a small notebook. Jack believes that trying new things keeps life fresh. Also, the manager gave an unambiguous instruction: finish the report today.

Jack has practiced football for three years and won a prize last term. Jack is saving money to buy a ticket to Paris. There are always more possibilities than we expect. Also, a pedal board the size of a suitcase.

There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. Jack prefers cloudy weather when running in the bookstore. The library serves as a national document depository.
Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. Tom always says that small steps matter more than big plans. On Friday evenings, Jack reviews the notes from class.
